drhp.business: Emami Realty Limited develops residential, commercial and mixed-use real estate projects, concentrated in and around Kolkata. It has one reportable business segment (real estate development) and one geographical segment (within India), targeting upper-mid and premium/luxury homebuyers and commercial occupiers.

drhp.expansion: The Company's near-term expansion pipeline is centred on advancing its five ongoing projects (Emami Aamod, Emami Aastha and Emami Business Bay among them), with Emami Business Bay expected to complete in FY 2026-27. Subject to necessary approvals, the Company intends to launch three new projects: Emami Miraai at SIPCOT, Chennai (~14 lakh sq ft saleable area), Emami Avaan at Liluah (~8 lakh sq ft saleable area), and Emami Vana at Buda, Jhansi (~45.5 lakh sq ft saleable area, proposed for phased launch). Beyond these, the Company is pursuing several other development opportunities at various stages of design, planned for launch in ensuing financial years. Strategically, the roadmap for 2026-2029 begins with monetising existing land banks before pursuing new land acquisitions and joint ventures, with West Bengal as the primary theatre of expansion.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Company expects the residential real estate market to remain stable in FY27, supported by steady urbanization, rising household incomes and continued government emphasis on infrastructure and housing-linked policy support; premium and high-end housing expected to continue attracting the greatest developer focus.
- West Bengal viewed as an underappreciated opportunity given historically slower capital formation and industrialisation, with a change in state government regime seen as an inflection point that could accelerate large-scale project implementation and strengthen investor confidence.
- Kolkata's emergence as a destination for Global Capability Centres, IT/ITES ecosystem and international corporate offices, plus metro-led infrastructure development, cited as demand drivers for housing in the Kolkata Metropolitan Region.
- Company continues to focus on timely execution of ongoing projects and disciplined capital allocation to sustain its growth trajectory.
- Cumulative bookings as on 31 March 2026 reached 30% in Emami Aamod, 82% in Emami Aastha and 98% in Emami Business Bay.
- Emami Business Bay is expected to be completed during FY 2026-27.
- Company is actively pursuing several other development opportunities at various stages of design and development, planned for launch in ensuing financial years.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company's near-term expansion pipeline is centred on advancing its five ongoing projects (Emami Aamod, Emami Aastha and Emami Business Bay among them), with Emami Business Bay expected to complete in FY 2026-27. Subject to necessary approvals, the Company intends to launch three new projects: Emami Miraai at SIPCOT, Chennai (~14 lakh sq ft saleable area), Emami Avaan at Liluah (~8 lakh sq ft saleable area), and Emami Vana at Buda, Jhansi (~45.5 lakh sq ft saleable area, proposed for phased launch). Beyond these, the Company is pursuing several other development opportunities at various stages of design, planned for launch in ensuing financial years. Strategically, the roadmap for 2026-2029 begins with monetising existing land banks before pursuing new land acquisitions and joint ventures, with West Bengal as the primary theatre of expansion.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Project execution continues to rely heavily on manual labour, leaving timelines exposed to workforce availability and to the rise in wage costs that followed the labour law changes introduced in November 2025.
- Inconsistent approval processes and regulatory frameworks across states remain a recurring source of project delays and cost overruns.
- Sustained price appreciation over recent years has strained affordability for first-time and middle-income buyers, contributing to a moderation in overall sales volumes even as demand in premium and luxury segments held firm.
- Developers slower to adopt PropTech, digital sales tools and green building practices risk losing competitive ground, as such adoption requires upfront capital and workforce upskilling that can be difficult to fund.
- The Company has taken debt to finance its working capital, exposing it to interest rate risk since a portion of borrowings is at variable rates.
- The Company is affected by price volatility of certain commodities/real estate, as its operating activities require ongoing development of real estate.
- Business is inherently exposed to shifts in interest rate movements, regulatory change, project-level demand-supply balance, and availability of financing for both developers and homebuyers.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Roadmap for 2026-2029 rests on two sequential, de-risked phases: first, internal asset monetisation to extract value from existing land banks and build a growth-ready balance sheet by 2026-27; then, new land acquisitions and joint-venture opportunities funded by internally generated capital.
- West Bengal is the primary theatre of planned expansion, leveraging headquarters proximity and brand equity in Kolkata.
- Portfolio has consciously moved upmarket, targeting an 80% residential / 20% commercial mix weighted toward upper-mid and premium/luxury segments rather than the mass-market Rs 50-80 lakh category, to capture rising purchasing power of the IT/GCC/corporate workforce converging on Kolkata.
- Sustainability commitments (use of fly ash to reduce cement content, chemical curing methods to conserve water) are positioned as part of the strategy.
